tasks.short: Match applications to the vacancy must-haves

today.trigger: Applications land on an open vacancy in Recruitee, or a hiring manager asks why nobody has been put forward.
steps: Read the vacancy must-haves: site, shift, certificates (forklift, VCA, code 95, food safety), language, and CAO function group.
Read each CV, motivation, and certificate copy in Recruitee, including people passed in by an agency.
Set aside applicants who cannot work the shift or the site, or who lack a stated certificate.
Check AFAS when a name looks like a former employee or an internal mover.
Hand the hiring manager a shortlist and park the rest.
drudgery: Rereading the same warehouse CV shape all week
Chasing missing certificate photos and unreadable scans
Re-screening a pile after the manager changes the shift
today.time_sinks: Peaks when Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo are hiring at once and a few hundred applications sit unread, mixed with paper forms from open evenings.

lenses.faster: The first pass on certificates, shift, site, and right-to-work documents leaves the recruiter's day. What remains is a short list with the reason each person is on it or off it.
lenses.autonomous: A new application in Recruitee starts the match the same day. The pile no longer waits until someone remembers to open it.
lenses.ambitious: If matching cost a tenth, every application would be scored the same day on the same must-haves, in quiet weeks and in the August peak, and people who just missed would be ready for the next similar vacancy.
lenses.joy: The repeated warehouse CVs drop away. What is left is the unusual profile and a sharper talk with the manager about who is worth meeting.
lenses.options: Five shortlists for one vacancy, each under a different must-have set, show what a diploma rule or a nights-only rule does to the number of people left.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter maintains the must-have list, the document checks, and a weekly sample of overrides, and stops reading every CV as the job.
reach: HR Administrator: spot rehires and thin files before an offer is drafted
Learning and Development Specialist: see a missing VCA or forklift certificate while the person is still an applicant
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: take structured match reasons into the nightly extract

tasks.human_edge: Judgement on borderline people, any knock-out that is not a written must-have, and the call when a scan, a name change, or a prior employment record is unclear.
tasks.pattern_why: An application is unstructured and the useful result is a structured pass, fail, or review against must-haves a person can check. The agent reads Recruitee, AFAS, and the certificate files, and a rejection only counts after the recruiter confirms the batch.

in_practice.trigger: An application reaches the new stage in Recruitee, or a vacancy is approved with its must-haves filled in.
steps: Load the vacancy must-haves from the approved intake, split by warehouse CAO or CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer.
Read the CV and attachments into fields: certificates, shifts, site, language, right to work, earlier Noordhaven employment.
Apply the hard rules, then rank the rest with a short reason tied to a vacancy line.
Put clear misses in a daily rejection batch and unclear cases in a review queue.
Write the result and the rule version back to the candidate in Recruitee.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter confirms the day's objective rejection batch and decides every review case before anyone is rejected or sent to a manager. A candidate can ask for a person to reopen the file.
data_needed: Vacancy must-haves and CAO function group
Application text and certificate files
Prior employment flag from AFAS
Consent and retention status of the application
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee timeline and a SharePoint screening log: rule version, fields used, outcome, and who overrode it.

evidence.claim: CV parsing and matching against structured job criteria is a current product, including the Dutch vendor Textkernel.
Recruitee holds the application, the vacancy, and the pipeline stage a match result can be written back to.
AFAS Profit holds employee history, so a former employee can be recognised before a new offer.
Software that filters or ranks job applicants falls under the high-risk employment rules of the EU AI Act and needs human oversight, logging, and a bias check.

risks: A scanned or handwritten certificate is misread and a qualified person is rejected.
A criterion that looks neutral, such as years in the Netherlands or full availability, tracks age, disability, or nationality and is hard to defend under equal-treatment law.
The works council has not agreed a recruitment rule that screens people this way, or the DPIA is missing, and the process has to be switched off.
Agency candidates and open-evening paper forms never enter Recruitee, so the match covers only part of the real inflow.
research_questions: What share of applications fail on a written must-have, and what share need judgement?
How many applications arrive as searchable text, and how many are phone photos, scans, or job-fair paper?
Will the works council and the privacy officer accept a daily batch confirmation as the human oversight, with a right to reopen?
On the same vacancy type, do people hired from the ranked list differ at day 90 on retention, absence, and manager satisfaction?

tasks.short: Tell applicants the pay, shifts, and the job

today.trigger: An applicant asks what the work, pay, or hours really are, or a recruiter needs to explain the role before an interview.
steps: Look up the vacancy text and the CAO scale the manager and Compensation and Benefits agreed.
Explain duties, ploegen, allowances, travel, and site conditions from memory or a SharePoint sheet.
Answer the follow-up in Outlook or by phone.
Correct anything a hiring manager said that does not match the CAO or the vacancy.
systems: AFAS Profit salary tables via Compensation and Benefits or a spreadsheet
drudgery: Repeating the night-shift pattern and the scale explanation many times a week
Searching for the current allowance because the vacancy, the Excel sheet, and the manager disagree
today.time_sinks: Long mail threads about pay that should have been a single approved figure, and calls that restart from zero because nothing was logged on the candidate.

lenses.faster: Standard questions on duties, scale, ploegen, travel, and certificates go out as approved text the same day. The recruiter handles only the questions that depend on this person.
lenses.autonomous: A question on a known topic, received in Recruitee or Outlook, is matched to an approved block and queued without a reminder.
lenses.ambitious: If a correct answer cost a tenth, every applicant would get the same plain account of the job, the roster, and the scale before they travel to a site, in the language that site actually hires in.
lenses.joy: The repeated explanation of nights in Venlo and the same allowance table goes. The conversation about whether this life fits this person stays.
lenses.options: The same vacancy can carry three plain versions: day shift, two-shift, and nights, each with the right allowances, so the applicant reacts to a real roster.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter keeps the answer library current with Compensation and Benefits and the sites, and reviews a weekly sample, and stops being the person who retypes the scale.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: publish the scale and allowance answers warehouse applicants actually ask
HR Business Partner: brief hiring managers so local pay promises match the CAO

tasks.human_edge: Any answer that depends on this person's inschaling, a medical or accommodation question, a competing offer, or a promise the approved text does not contain.
tasks.pattern_why: The question is unstructured, but a safe reply is one approved block or an escalation. The model may only choose a block that Compensation and Benefits and the recruiter have already signed. It does not write pay or conditions in its own words.

in_practice.trigger: An applicant asks about duties, pay, benefits, hours, or the site, by mail, via the vacancy page, or in a Recruitee message.
steps: Classify the question against the approved library for that vacancy and CAO.
If one block matches, attach the current scale, roster, and certificate lines for that site.
If nothing matches, or the question is about this person's pay, health, or a special arrangement, put it in the recruiter queue with the vacancy facts beside it.
Send the matched block in the applicant's language where a translation has been approved.
Log which block went out and which version of the CAO table it used.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter sends every reply that is not an exact approved block. A weekly sample of auto-sent answers is checked against the current CAO tables.
data_needed: Approved answer blocks per role family, site, and CAO
Current scale, ploegentoeslag, and travel rules from Compensation and Benefits
Vacancy text the manager signed
Language of the applicant
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee message log and a SharePoint register of answer blocks with owner, version, and date.

evidence.claim: Recruitee can send a stored message on a candidate and keep it on the application.
Outlook templates in Microsoft 365 already send fixed text a recruiter has written.
Warehouse and transport pay at this company is bounded by the relevant CAO, so a figure can be checked against a table rather than composed.
A model that writes pay or allowances in its own words will sometimes invent a figure; selecting an approved block avoids that class of error.

risks: An outdated allowance or the wrong CAO (transport rates sent to a warehouse role, or the reverse) becomes a promise that is painful to unwind.
Candidates who wanted a person before accepting nights read a fast standard answer as indifference and drop out.
A translation drifts from the Dutch CAO text and two languages promise different hours or pay.
Answers about health, pregnancy, or disability are pushed into a standard block and the company breaches the rules on medical questions.
research_questions: What share of applicant questions are already answered by the vacancy, the CAO excerpt, or the benefits page?
How often does a recruiter or manager state pay, allowances, or shifts that Compensation and Benefits later corrects?
Do applicants who receive a fast standard answer accept offers at a different rate from those who speak to a recruiter first?
Which languages cover nearly all applicants at each site, and who signs those translations?

tasks.short: Choose who goes to the manager and recommend a hire

today.trigger: Enough people sit in review, or interviews are done and the manager wants a name.
steps: Compare interviewed applicants on the Recruitee notes and scorecard.
Check internal candidates in AFAS for role history and current employment.
Talk the choice through with the hiring manager on Teams.
Recommend hire, hold, or reject, and write why.
Record the manager's decision, including when it differs from the scorecard.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same comparison because notes sit in Recruitee, mail, and chat
Chasing managers who watched the interviews and never scored them
today.time_sinks: Waiting on manager feedback, then rewriting the recommendation the night before a start-date promise.

lenses.faster: The comparison note, the gaps against the must-haves, and the record of similar hires who stayed to day 90 are already on one page when the manager call starts.
lenses.autonomous: When the last interview scorecard is in, the brief builds itself and waits on the candidate. The recruiter is pinged, and does not assemble it from three systems.
lenses.ambitious: If a sound recommendation cost a tenth, every hire, including peak-season order pickers, would have a written reason and a day-90 check, which today only the harder office roles receive.
lenses.joy: Copying notes into a comparison mail goes. The judgement call with the manager, and telling the person the outcome properly, stays.
lenses.options: The manager sees the leading person plus the next two, with what changes if night-shift flexibility or a missing certificate is weighted differently.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter improves the scorecard and the briefing habit of managers, and spends less of the week rewriting one-off comparisons.
reach: HR Business Partner: run the decision meeting when a site's hires keep leaving before day 90
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: attach a day-90 outcome to each recommendation after the fact

tasks.human_edge: The recommendation itself, especially when evidence is thin, two managers disagree, or a protected ground could be touched by the reason.
tasks.pattern_why: Choosing a person is the recruiter's and the manager's decision, and the volumes per role are often too small for a model to decide. The help that holds up is a brief grounded in the scorecard, the must-haves, and what happened to similar hires.

in_practice.trigger: All required scorecards for a vacancy are in, or a manager asks for a recommendation.
steps: Pull scorecards, must-haves, certificate status, and shift acceptance from Recruitee.
Add AFAS facts for internal candidates and any earlier employment.
Draft a one-page brief: who meets the must-haves, what is missing, and how similar past hires looked at day 90 where the extract has that link.
Sit with the manager, record the decision and the reason in the manager's words.
Send the decision to the status step only after the manager has confirmed.
in_practice.human_gate: No hire, reject, or refer is final until the recruiter and the hiring manager both confirm the reason. The model does not vote.
data_needed: Completed scorecards tied to vacancy must-haves
Certificate and shift fields
Day-90 retention and absence for earlier hires in the same role family, where the join exists
Manager identity and decision
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee scorecard and a recommendation note that stores the reason, the manager, and the date.

evidence.claim: Recruitee stores interview feedback and pipeline stage, which is enough to draft a comparison.
Power BI on a nightly AFAS extract can show whether earlier hires are still employed and what their absence looks like.
A model that recommends who to hire is high-risk employment use, and a human decision with a written reason is the defensible setup.
With a few hires per role family per year, a statistical ranking will often be weaker than a short structured scorecard.

risks: The brief overweights fluent Dutch or a familiar employer and pushes out older workers or people trained abroad.
A manager treats the draft ranking as the decision and stops looking at the evidence.
Day-90 numbers from a different site or a different shift are shown as if they predict this hire.
Internal candidates' absence history is shown more deeply than external candidates' data, and the comparison becomes unfair and hard to explain under the AVG.
research_questions: When recruiter and manager disagree today, whose choice looks better at day 90?
Which scorecard items are filled in on most hires, and which are blank or mean different things per site?
Is the number of hires per role family large enough to check a criterion, or only large enough for a checklist?
What does the company tell applicants today about how the decision is made, and does a written AI brief change that notice?

tasks.short: Tell applicants where their application stands

today.trigger: A stage changes, a candidate mails to ask for news, or someone has sat in a stage for weeks.
steps: Open the candidate in Recruitee and read the stage.
Send a template, or type a short mail in Outlook.
After the manager decides, tell the people who were rejected.
Answer replies, complaints, and people who ask for feedback.
drudgery: Closing people who were never told no
Copying the same rejection text by hand
today.time_sinks: The backlog of job-fair and agency names with a missing email, and rejections that wait until the recruiter has a quiet hour that does not come.

lenses.faster: A stage change sends the matching status mail the same day. The recruiter no longer spends the afternoon on 'any news?' replies.
lenses.autonomous: Moving an application to 'in review', 'interview', 'rejected', or 'hired' triggers the approved mail. Silence no longer depends on a reminder.
lenses.ambitious: If status mail cost a tenth, every applicant, including peak-season and job-fair inflow, would hear a clear outcome within the time the company is willing to promise.
lenses.joy: The chase mail goes. A personal note after a real interview, and a careful reply to someone who is upset, stays.
lenses.options: Rejection texts can exist in a few approved tones and languages, still the same facts, so a Venlo nights rejection and an office rejection are both fit to send.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter sets the stage rules, the clock for each stage, and the wording, and checks exceptions, and stops being the status inbox.
reach: HR Administrator: start the contract pack only after the hired status has actually gone to the candidate
Hiring managers via the HR Business Partner: a clock on scorecards so 'in review' does not last a month

tasks.human_edge: A rejection after a conversation, a complaint, a request for feedback, and any mail where the stage in Recruitee may be wrong.
tasks.pattern_why: The input is a stage the recruiter already set, and the output is an approved sentence the company can stand behind. Rules do that. A model adds wording risk without adding a checkable fact.

in_practice.trigger: An application changes stage in Recruitee, or it has sat in a stage longer than the agreed number of days.
steps: Map the stage to one approved template and language.
Check that an email exists and that the stage move was made by a person, not by a failed import.
Send the mail and write the time on the candidate timeline.
If the stage is 'rejected after interview' or the candidate has replied before, hold for the recruiter.
Chase the owner of any application that is over the stage clock.
in_practice.human_gate: Templates are approved once by the recruiter and HR. After that, standard status mail goes by itself. The recruiter writes rejections that follow an interview, handles replies, and corrects a wrong stage before a mail goes.
data_needed: Stage definitions and the template for each
A working email and language
The stage clock per vacancy type
Flag for interview already held
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee stage history and the sent-message log, including template version.

evidence.claim: Recruitee can send a template email when a candidate moves stage and store that message on the candidate.
Outlook templates cover the same kind of repeated status text inside Microsoft 365.
The Dutch NVP Sollicitatiecode expects applicants to be told where they stand and not left open without an end.

risks: A wrong stage sends a rejection or an offer signal to the wrong person.
Job-fair applicants with no email still sit in silence while the system reports that status mail is done.
A blunt template raises complaints, or a warm template implies the door is open when the role is closed.
Mail in the wrong language looks like no answer to a large share of the warehouse inflow.
research_questions: What share of status contacts are a standard stage message that expects no personal reply?
Does every live applicant in Recruitee have a correct email and a stage, including agency and job-fair names?
How many complaints a year are about silence or a wrong outcome, and which stages produce them?
Which outcomes does company practice, or the NVP Sollicitatiecode as applied here, require a named person to send?

tasks.short: Find people for open roles from pools, agencies, and boards

today.trigger: The shortlist is thin, a site forecasts a busy period, or a hard shift has been open too long.
steps: Search the Recruitee pool and recent people who nearly made it.
Ask managers for referrals and check which flex workers the agencies already have on site.
Refresh the vacancy on the boards and on werk.nl where the company uses them.
For office roles, search LinkedIn. For warehouse roles, plan an open evening or a site fair.
Approach people and log the source, often in loose notes.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same search and pasting the vacancy into another board
Writing the same outreach mail to people who were already told no last season
today.time_sinks: Office-style searching spent on warehouse roles that are actually filled through agencies, flex workers already on site, and local fairs.

lenses.faster: The internal pool, recent near-misses, referrals, and the agency names already on that site are listed before any new board is opened.
lenses.autonomous: When a vacancy is approved and the number of qualified applicants drops under the agreed line, the search list is built without waiting for a recruiter to notice.
lenses.ambitious: If search cost a tenth, every hard shift would have a warm list before the vacancy opened: flex workers ready for direct hire, referrers, and people who already consented to be contacted.
lenses.joy: Copying vacancy text from board to board goes. Talking to a referrer, a community fair, and a good agency contact stays.
lenses.options: Three source mixes per vacancy, with last year's day-90 retention and rough cost, let the site choose before money goes to another board.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter decides which sources are allowed to run for which role family, and stops treating every vacancy as a fresh search from scratch.
reach: HR Business Partner: turn a thin pipeline into a site coverage problem early
Learning and Development Specialist: see which sourced people still need a certificate before they can start
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: flag when a source is dry because the scale, not the advert, is the block

tasks.human_edge: The relationship with referrers, agencies, and local fairs, and the decision to contact a named person.
tasks.pattern_why: The search crosses several systems and the output is a list the recruiter can accept or cut. Contacting someone who did not apply is a privacy-sensitive act, so the list does not become an approach until the recruiter approves it.

in_practice.trigger: A vacancy is approved and qualified applicants are below the number set for that role family, or a site forecast shows a gap.
steps: List internal pool matches, earlier applicants with current consent, and open referrals.
Add flex workers the agencies have named for that site, without copying their whole file into Recruitee.
Draft outreach from the approved vacancy text, in the right language.
Show the recruiter the list, the source, and the legal basis for each name.
After approval, log who was contacted and the source on the vacancy.
in_practice.human_gate: Nobody is contacted until the recruiter approves the batch. People who never applied are approved name by name.
data_needed: Role family, site, shift, and must-haves
Consent and date for anyone kept in a pool
Agency bench lists the contract allows the company to see
Past hire counts by source
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee source field and a SharePoint search log: who was proposed, the basis for contact, and who approved the approach.

evidence.claim: Recruitee talent pools can hold earlier applicants and record the source of a candidate.
LinkedIn Recruiter searches professional profiles and is a poor fit for forklift and order-picker hiring.
Employers publish vacancies on werk.nl through the UWV employer channel.
Contacting someone who never applied needs a purpose, a notice, and usually a recorded basis under the AVG.

risks: People are contacted from an old pool after consent has lapsed, or agency workers are approached outside the agency contract.
A search trained on last year's hires copies a narrow profile and misses older workers and career switchers.
Boards are refreshed automatically with vacancy text that still contains an exclusionary line a manager once added.
Time moves from boards to tools while the roles were always going to be filled at a fair or from flex already on site.
research_questions: Which sources produced hires still in post and productive at day 90, by role family and site, over the last two years?
What share of search time is internal pool, referral, and flex-to-perm, and what share is external boards and fairs?
Do the CAO, the works council, or company rules require internal staff and current flex workers to see a vacancy before external search?
Will the privacy officer accept pool reuse and agency-bench search on the basis the company uses today?

tasks.short: Check that selection criteria are fair and useful

today.trigger: A role stays open, a manager wants to raise the bar, or several hires leave before day 90.
steps: Read the must-haves and the interview form used on recent vacancies.
Ask People Analytics for a funnel or build a rough count in Excel.
Compare who was rejected with who was hired and who stayed, where that is easy to see.
Propose a change to the HR Business Partner or the HR Director.
Update the SharePoint template if the change is accepted.
drudgery: Collecting vacancy texts that were never written the same way twice
Arguing about a diploma or a fluency line with no link to the work
today.time_sinks: Criteria debates that restart on every vacancy because nothing is written as a rule with an owner.

lenses.faster: Pass rates by stage, the must-haves actually used, and day-90 outcomes for that role family are on one page before the criteria meeting.
lenses.autonomous: A role family that misses its 90-day retention or runs over its time-to-hire opens a criteria review. The recruiter does not wait for a complaint.
lenses.ambitious: If a proper review cost a tenth, every role family would keep a short criteria sheet that is checked twice a year against retention, absence, and time to fill, which the company does not do as a habit today.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding the argument from old vacancy PDFs goes. Deciding, with managers, what the work really requires stays.
lenses.options: Three criterion sets, with how many of last year's applicants would have remained and how those hires turned out, make the cost of a diploma or a fluency rule visible.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter owns the criteria register for hiring, together with People Analytics, and stops editing one vacancy at a time with no memory.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: keep the funnel and day-90 view reliable enough to judge a criterion
HR Director: take a selection rule to the works council when it is a real change in hiring policy
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: map criteria to the right CAO function group

tasks.human_edge: The decision to change a criterion, and the conversation with managers, the HR Director, and the works council about what the company is willing to require.
tasks.pattern_why: The output is advice to change a rule that affects who gets work, done a few times a month with other people. A draft comparison helps. Publishing a new criterion is a human decision under equal-treatment duties and, where it is a hiring regulation, the works council.

in_practice.trigger: A role family misses the agreed time-to-hire or 90-day retention, a manager asks to add a criterion, or the half-year review is due.
steps: List the must-haves used on vacancies in that role family over the last year.
Compute stage pass rates and, where the join exists, day-90 retention and absence, with small numbers suppressed.
Flag criteria that removed many people and show no link to staying or to a legal certificate.
Draft a revision: drop, keep, or add, with the job duty that justifies each line.
The recruiter walks it through with the HR Business Partner and the HR Director before any template changes.
in_practice.human_gate: No must-have changes on the live vacancy template until the HR Director agrees, and the works council is involved where the change is a hiring rule.
data_needed: Must-haves as recorded, not as remembered
Stage outcomes by role family and site
Day-90 retention and absence where the person was hired
Legal or customer requirements such as VCA, code 95, or food safety
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint criteria register: role family, criterion, owner, reason, date, and who approved the change.

evidence.claim: Power BI can calculate stage counts and retention once Recruitee outcomes and AFAS employment dates are in the same extract.
COTAN rates psychological and selection tests in the Netherlands; a home-made test usually has no such rating.
The Algemene wet gelijke behandeling restricts criteria that track protected grounds unless the job itself requires them.
Recruitee and SharePoint already hold the vacancy texts and templates this review would read.

risks: Demographic fields are pulled into the analysis to 'check bias' and the company processes data the AVG does not allow for that purpose.
A criterion is dropped because the sample is small and noisy, and a real safety requirement goes with it.
Site managers keep a private extra requirement, so the register describes a process the floor does not use.
The review becomes a report on Power BI that never changes a template.
research_questions: Are must-haves written on each vacancy in a structured field, or only inside free text and old PDFs?
Can People Analytics join criterion, hire, and day-90 retention without special-category data?
Which current criteria have no link to the work, to a certificate, or to staying, and which are required by a customer or the CAO?
Does the works council expect consent before selection criteria or scorecards change?

tasks.short: Plan how we fill the roles we see coming

today.trigger: Quarterly headcount talks, a site forecast, or a warehouse living on expensive flex.
steps: Pull open roles and time to hire from Recruitee and the Power BI extract.
Ask the three sites what they need next quarter, including peak flex.
Sketch a mix of direct hire, flex-to-perm, and agency cover.
Talk it through with the HR Director and the HR Business Partners.
Rewrite the Excel sheet when agency numbers and AFAS headcount do not match.
drudgery: Reconciling three agency files with AFAS headcount by hand
Chasing site managers for numbers that arrive after the plan was due
today.time_sinks: A plan that is stale by the time Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo have all replied, so hiring still starts when a shift is already short.

lenses.faster: Open roles, starters, agency hours, and last year's time to hire sit in one working view before the planning meeting, with the gaps marked.
lenses.autonomous: A site forecast or a flex order that crosses an agreed line opens an updated hiring view. The recruiter does not wait for the quarterly meeting to see the gap.
lenses.ambitious: If a plan cost a tenth, each site would keep a rolling 13-week view by role family, with direct hire, flex-to-perm, and agency as explicit choices, which today is assembled late and then abandoned.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding the spreadsheet goes. The argument about how exposed a site is willing to be, and which shifts are worth a permanent hire, stays.
lenses.options: Three mixes per site, with cost per person still productive at day 90, time to fill, and agency dependence, give the HR Director a real choice.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter designs the planning rhythm and the source rules, and spends the meeting on gaps and quality, not on collecting numbers.
reach: FP&A Analyst: cost a direct hire against agency spend for the same shift
HR Business Partner: turn the plan into manager-level vacancies while there is still time
Payroll Specialist: see starter peaks before the monthly pay cut-off
Learning and Development Specialist: reserve certificate training before day one

tasks.human_edge: The choice of mix: what the sites can absorb, what the works council climate will bear, and how far to depend on agencies.
tasks.pattern_why: The plan is a choice about cost, service, and people, made with the HR Director and the sites. Scenarios and a cleaned data view make that choice faster. They do not make it.

in_practice.trigger: The monthly site forecast arrives, a role family slips its fill-time, or agency hours on a shift cross the line the HR Director set.
steps: Combine AFAS headcount, Recruitee open vacancies, and agency hours into one view per site and role family.
Draft three mixes for the next 13 weeks: direct hire, flex-to-perm, and stay on agency.
Attach last year's time to hire, 90-day retention, and a rough cost, and label missing figures as missing.
Review the draft with the HR Business Partners before it goes to the HR Director.
Write the agreed mix back as vacancies to open, agency orders to keep, and training seats to book.
in_practice.human_gate: The HR Director agrees the mix. Site managers agree the vacancies that will actually be opened. Nothing is posted from the draft.
data_needed: Headcount and leavers by site and role
Open vacancies and stage speed
Agency hours and known bench
Certificate lead times from Learning and Development
Any hiring pause agreed with the works council
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint hiring-plan page with the version that was agreed, and the Power BI page it was drawn from.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit holds headcount and Recruitee holds open vacancies, which are the two counts a hiring plan has to reconcile.
Power BI is already how this company looks at HR and finance figures once they are in the nightly extract.
Agency portals hold flex hours and orders outside Recruitee, so a plan that ignores them misstates warehouse coverage.

risks: A neat scenario hides a bad agency feed and the site hires permanent staff it does not need after the peak.
The plan assumes certificate seats and payroll cut-offs that Learning and Development and Payroll cannot meet.
Managers nod at the plan and still open vacancies one by one the old way.
Cost per productive hire is compared on agency invoices versus salary only, and the CAO allowances and the cost of early leavers are left out.
research_questions: Is there a volume forecast per site each week that hiring can follow, or do vacancies open only after a shift is short?
What is the full cost of a direct hire still productive at day 90 versus flex-then-hire versus staying on agency, including allowances and fees?
Do site managers open the vacancies a plan names, and what happened to the last plan?
How many weeks before a start does Learning and Development need to finish VCA, forklift, or food-safety training?

tasks.short: Set and run the checks we use on applicants

today.trigger: A role needs a practical check, a certificate must be shown, or someone suggests adding a test.
steps: Agree with the hiring manager and Learning and Development what will be checked.
Collect a certificate copy, or book a practical on site with a team lead.
Record pass or fail in Recruitee, often as a note.
See later whether the check rejected people who would have been fine, or passed people who struggled in the first weeks.
drudgery: Chasing certificate photos and typing pass or fail from a team lead's mail
Rescheduling practicals when the warehouse cannot spare a person
today.time_sinks: Practicals that depend on one busy team lead, and debates about adding a personality test nobody on the team is qualified to use.

lenses.faster: Certificate checks and a standard practical checklist are ready with the vacancy, and results land on the candidate without a scavenger hunt through mail.
lenses.autonomous: A vacancy with a required practical or certificate opens the checklist and the evidence request as soon as the person passes the must-have screen.
lenses.ambitious: If a sound check cost a tenth, every safety-critical role would use the same short practical, scored the same way on all three sites, which today depends on which team lead is on shift.
lenses.joy: Retyping certificate dates and chasing lost photos goes. Watching a real practical and deciding a borderline result stays.
lenses.options: Two or three practical tasks per role family can be tried on paper against last year's early leavers before any of them is imposed on applicants.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter, with Learning and Development, keeps a small set of job-related checks and retires the rest, and stops inventing a new test per manager.
reach: Learning and Development Specialist: turn a missing certificate into training before day one, where the role allows a start on that basis
HR Business Partner: agree with each site which roles truly need a practical
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: keep a certificate requirement aligned with the function group

tasks.human_edge: Giving the practical, judging a borderline performance, and any decision that touches health or a psychological instrument.
tasks.pattern_why: A check that decides who is hired has to be job-related and possible to explain. Drafting a practical checklist and comparing results with day-90 outcomes can be assisted. Administering it, and anything medical or psychological, stays with a qualified person.

in_practice.trigger: A role family is marked as needing a certificate check or a practical, or a manager asks for a new test.
steps: Show the existing protocol: certificates, practical tasks, and who may score them.
If a new check is proposed, draft tasks from the real work and set aside anything medical, personality-based, or based on face, voice, or emotion.
Collect certificate evidence on the application and internal completions from Studytube.
A named site assessor runs the practical and records scores on the checklist.
Twice a year, compare results with day-90 retention and early absence, and drop checks that only add delay.
in_practice.human_gate: A person who is allowed to assess that task signs every pass or fail. No new test goes live until the HR Director accepts it, with Learning and Development, and the works council where it changes the selection rules.
data_needed: The protocol per role family and the certificate names that satisfy it
Assessor name and score
Studytube completions for internal candidates
Day-90 outcome for people who passed
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee result field and a SharePoint protocol sheet per role family, with version and assessor.

evidence.claim: Studytube records enrolment and completion for courses the company assigns, including safety courses.
COTAN rates tests used for selection in the Netherlands, and the Wet medische keuringen limits pre-employment medical checks.
The EU AI Act treats selection systems as high-risk and restricts emotion recognition of workers.
Recruitee can store a structured result on a candidate if the field is set up.

risks: A video or personality score is added because it is easy to buy, and it is neither job-related nor something this team may administer.
A practical on a live shift is rushed in peak season and scored differently in Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo.
External forklift and VCA cards are treated as if Studytube held them, so qualified people look unqualified.
A failed practical is stored without a reason and cannot be explained to the applicant or the works council.
research_questions: Which checks are in use today, per role family, and which are required by law or by a customer?
Do practical scores add anything to day-90 retention once certificates, shift acceptance, and the interview scorecard are known?
Who on or outside the team is qualified to administer any psychological instrument, and is one in use?
Can a work sample be run at each site in peak season without depending on a single team lead?

role.altitude: The recruiter stops being the inbox for every CV and status mail and becomes the person who designs how Noordhaven hires: the must-haves, the sources, the words applicants can rely on, and the check that a hire was productive and still here at day 90.
reach: HR Business Partner: get vacancy intake and manager scorecards agreed before a role opens
Learning and Development Specialist: put VCA, forklift, or food-safety training in week one where the hire still needs it
HR Administrator: open the AFAS contract file from a complete accepted offer
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: keep source, speed, and day-90 retention trustworthy in the nightly extract
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: confirm CAO inschaling before the offer leaves
FP&A Analyst: compare agency cost with a direct hire who stays to day 90
Payroll Specialist: receive starters with complete contract data before the monthly cut-off
role.ceiling_note: These tasks are about seven tenths of the recruiter year. The hours that can leave the week sit mainly in screening and status mail. Interviews, open evenings on three sites, manager delay, agency seasonality of 150 to 300 flex workers, and the duty to keep a person on selection decisions put a floor under the role. Two people cannot both be at peak-season fairs and run the controls. Spare hours should go to hard-to-fill shifts and day-90 quality before anyone treats this as a reason to shrink the team.
skills_to_grow: Write must-haves that can be checked, and tie them to day-90 retention and absence
Set Recruitee stages, templates, and logs the privacy officer and the works council can audit
Explain CAO scales, ploegen, and allowances without promising outside the signed table
Read time to hire, source, offer acceptance, and day-90 retention by site and role family
Review a batch of automated rejections and reopen a case when an applicant asks
Judge direct hire, flex-to-perm, and agency on cost per person still productive at day 90
role.ambitious_version: The two recruiters keep Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo staffed to a rolling plan. Matching, status messages, and standard job facts run on approved rules with a human gate. Their own week goes to hard shifts, to managers whose hires do not stay, and to proof of which sources produce people who are productive and still here after 90 days.
